conclusion: the refusal happens before anything is sent: the bridge answers host_conversation_unproven and the daemon records no command request for that call. The matrix claim is now measured rather than inferred from where the check sits in the code.
method: the daemon writes a uvicorn access log at <project>/.tsunagou/local/daemon.log recording every HTTP request. Line counts were taken around two calls, with the second as a control so that an absent line means something.
not_measured: whether a refused call would leave a trace on a host whose bridge talks to a different daemon transport

control_allowed_call.case: the enrolled conversation with its own overlay
control_allowed_call.reading: a permitted call does leave a commands line, which is what makes the absence above meaningful rather than an artefact of the log not recording that route

refused_call.case: a brand-new conversation handed the enrolled overlay
refused_call.reading: the two added lines are unrelated health polls; no POST /api/v1/commands/... appears, so the call never reached the daemon

why: the runtime binding row said the bridge refuses 'before contacting the daemon'. That was read off the code placement of the check, not observed, and the fourth self-review pass flagged it as a scope claim the evidence did not cover.
withdrawn: HISTORICAL: the refusal measured here came from a guard that has since been DELETED (see runtime-binding.json). It describes an attempt, not the current source.
